payload.viable_set:
KILLER CRITERION — MET, with two viable candidates rather than an argued absence of alternatives.

THE FRONT: {X1 fit-per-job, X2 one-searcher}. Neither dominates.
  X1 — a packaged searcher answers the working tree, version-control grep answers the record. Better at structured output, native bounding, and reaching a source that is not a repository at all.
  X2 — version-control grep answers both, in --untracked mode for the working tree. Better at installability (no dependency; version control is already a hard prerequisite) and simplicity (one mechanism, one subprocess, eight elements against nine).

HOW THIS KILLER CAME TO BE MET HONESTLY, recorded because the sequence is the evidence: the first pass chose X2 without applying its own freshness veto. The rewalk applied the veto and eliminated X2, leaving a front of one, and argued the no-alternatives case — which satisfies this killer's second branch. This gate's red team then PROBED the veto (run-3d8fb30546e5) and found the claim false: --untracked sees a file written and never staged, with line numbers, and context works alongside. X2 came back, and the killer is met by its FIRST branch.
Arguing away a candidate that is actually viable is the strongest form of decision theatre available, and this gate came within one probe of doing it.

X3 remains eliminated, and its elimination was never in question — it rests on a property of the situation (semantic selection has no ground truth here) rather than on an unprobed claim about a tool.
payload.complete_allocation:
All three candidates allocate every function F1-F36; none leaves one unallocated. They differ only where the chart left a real choice.

SHARED BY ALL, with identical allocation and interfaces: K3 alteration, K5 mechanical decision, K6 preservation and settings, K7 oblige the review, K8 share the judge, and the record-search half of K1.

WHERE THEY DIFFER:
  X1 — K1 splits into a working-tree element and a record element joined by ONE shared addressing contract. 9 elements, 14 inter-element edges, longest chain 4.
  X2 — K1 is a single element answering both, with a mode switch. 8 elements, 12 edges, chain 4.
  X3 — as X1 plus a scoring stage between rule storage and packet assembly. 9 elements, 15 edges, chain 5.

INTERFACES = INTER-CLUSTER EDGES, recorded per candidate. Two matter and are identical in all three:
  K4→K5 (contract) — a rule supplied to the agent and a rule enforced by a lint must be the same rule, or the machine says one thing and checks another.
  F33 and F34 inside ONE element — returning work and keeping its path back open. A candidate splitting them was deliberately never enumerated.

THAT SECOND INTERFACE EARNED ITSELF AGAIN DURING THIS GATE, and it belongs in the record rather than only in a note: the reopen used to reach this front damaged the walk twice. First it stranded a downstream join. Then the fix for that handed back join fuel for the state it was activating, so the state re-activated itself on completion and the walk stopped moving — visible on the board as two sequential states live at once. Both are fixed, covered by five tests, and promoted (c30f023, 221 passed / 0 failed in trunk). The allocation claim that F33 and F34 are one element is not a tidy preference; it is the shape of two measured failures.
payload.criteria_traced:
Nine criteria, each with definition, requirement lineage and weight. Two are vetoes, declared before any scoring so they cannot be traded away inside a total.

FROM REQUIREMENTS: C1←R1,R3,R5 · C2←R5,R6,R7 · C4←R3,R19,R28 · C6←R28 · C7←R14,R15,R37 · C8←R14 · C9←R8,R19,R31,R34.
FROM STAKEHOLDER TENSIONS: C3 from the owner's one-click bar (T6, owner versus engine over dependencies) · C5 from the no-duplicate-code ruling and R13 · C9 from T1, the walking agent versus the reviewing agent.

TWO NEED DEFENDING RATHER THAN LISTING.
  C5 was REWRITTEN this pass, not re-weighted. Under its first definition it produced the whole wrong architecture by treating two questions as one job. Its weight stays 5; it now requires naming the QUESTION both paths answer before it may rule anything out. A criterion that decides everything by itself is usually one that has been misdefined — and once corrected, C5 scores 5 for every candidate and discriminates between none of them, which is what a correctly drawn boundary looks like.
  C8 is weight 2 deliberately, set before any candidate was scored. Higher, and X3 wins on migration cost alone — which would mean caring more about not rewriting ten nodes than about whether the delivered rules are the right ones.
payload.front_recorded:
THE FRONT: {X1, X2}, with every score grounded in a measurement rather than an expectation.

WEIGHTED TOTALS (C3-C9): X1 136 · X2 124 · X3 113. Totals are recorded for completeness and are NOT the decision — M5 converges, and a twelve-point gap across seven criteria is not a mandate.

WHAT SEPARATES THE TWO SURVIVORS, in both directions:
  X1 wins C4 structured output, 5 against 3. The packaged searcher emits typed records with spans and submatch offsets. Version-control grep emits delimited text whose shape SHIFTS between modes — probed (run-1ae8b534b535 C/D): the working tree yields path / line / text, while a ref yields 'ref:path' / line / text, packing two identifiers into the field the other case uses for one. Our parser must branch, and a branching parser is where an edge case is silently mis-read.
  X1 also wins on reach: it can search a directory that is not a repository at all. X2 cannot — version-control grep needs a repository. This surfaced only when the examples were walked a second time, and it narrows R7 rather than breaking it, since declared external roots can still be READ without being searched.
  X2 wins C3 installability outright, 5 against 4: no dependency at all. X1 depends on a package resolving a per-platform binary, with NO fallback if it ever does not — an exposure the owner has accepted, but an exposure, and probe P1 established that the system-PATH route does not exist even on the owner's own machine.
  X2 also wins on simplicity: one subprocess, one failure mode to bound, eight elements against nine.

THE TRADE IN ONE LINE, so M5 inherits a question rather than a preference: X1 buys typed output and reach beyond the repository, at the cost of a dependency with no fallback. X2 buys zero dependencies and one moving part, at the cost of parsing risk and a narrower reach.

ELIMINATION — X3, dominated on C7 selection correctness (2 against 5, weight 5) against its advantage on C8 migration debt (5 against 3, weight 2).
  WHAT IT WAS BETTER AT, first: migration cost, decisively — nothing to rewrite, nothing to author going forward, and it works on rules written by someone who never heard of the selector. That is a real advantage for a method meant to be used by people who did not build it.
  WHY IT LOSES: semantic selection cannot be checked. A rule scoring highly against a state's statement may still be the wrong rule, and there is no ground truth here to tell them apart. Its failure mode is a wrong selection indistinguishable from a right one.
  NOT DISCARDED, DEFERRED: it is the natural fallback if declared applicability proves too burdensome to author, and the M5 spike should record what X3 WOULD have selected for the same states — nearly free then, impossible to reconstruct later.

RETRACTION HELD IN THE RECORD: the superseded fill eliminated X2 on the freshness veto. That claim is false and both fills remain readable, the first marked superseded.

STILL OPEN INSIDE BOTH SURVIVORS: the guidance selector's vocabulary — state ids, kinds, or tags. Orthogonal to the X1/X2 choice, and the M5 spike.
payload.feasibility_checked:
ROUGH CHECKS PER SURVIVOR, both now resting on probes rather than expectations.

X1 — FEASIBLE, with one accepted exposure.
  The packaged searcher ships per-platform binaries resolved through the dependency rather than the PATH; probe P1 showed the PATH route is unavailable even on the owner's own machine, so the package IS the delivery mechanism.
  THE EXPOSURE: if the package ever fails to resolve a binary on some platform there is no fallback. Logged as a risk, with a documented manual install as the only mitigation.
  Ref search proven by probe P2 including output shape. Bounding is ours at the boundary — an implementation obligation, not a feasibility question.

X2 — FEASIBLE, and BOTH residual unknowns from the last pass are now settled by probe rather than left as caveats (run-1ae8b534b535):
  IGNORE-RULE REACH — --untracked respects the ignore rules; a file inside an ignored dependency directory is skipped. --no-exclude-standard reaches it. So the default is the behaviour we want AND it is controllable. Resolved in X2's favour.
  OUTPUT-SHAPE STABILITY — the shape DIFFERS between modes, as described above. Resolved AGAINST X2, and it is why C4 scores 3.
  A THIRD, found by walking the examples again: X2 cannot search a source that is not a repository, because version-control grep requires one. Not fatal — external roots can be read — but it narrows what X2 delivers against R7 and need N1, and M5 must weigh it.

X3 — not on the front. Its feasibility was not carried further than the observation that its selection quality cannot be established without the spike, which is why it lost.

CROSS-CANDIDATE, whichever converges: the guidance selector's vocabulary is unresolved in both survivors, and probe P5 measured why it is not free — ten ledger nodes carry applicability, zero machine-state nodes do, and the field's content is prose written for a person. That is the M5 spike.
payload.verify_round:
BUILT IT RIGHT. The re-walked state opened and read; the three untouched inputs re-checked rather than assumed.

1. evaluate_set (second fill) — read against its claim. Claims: scores grounded in three named probes; front of two; X3's elimination unchanged. Verified: every score that MOVED from the superseded fill carries its reason (C1 for X2 on the untracked probe; C6 4→3 on native bounding; C9 2→4, because the score of 2 was punishing X2 for contradicting a measured failure when the contradiction was mine, not X2's). The probe references resolve to real runs in this session. HOLDS.
   ONE THING THE RE-FILL ADDED THAT I DID NOT ASK FOR, and it is the sign the re-walk was real rather than cosmetic: walking the examples a second time surfaced that X2 cannot search a non-repository source at all. That is a functional gap nobody had noticed across two passes, and it appeared only because the candidate was restored and re-examined instead of re-eliminated.

2. derive_criteria — NOT reopened, re-read. C1 remains correctly defined and correctly a veto; what was wrong was a factual claim about whether a candidate trips it. HOLDS.

3. partition_functions — NOT reopened, re-read, and its second strong claim was re-tested against fresh evidence rather than accepted: F33 and F34 must stay in one element. Since the last gate that claim has been vindicated twice more, by two distinct defects in the reopen path. HOLDS, and more strongly than when written.

4. enumerate_space — NOT reopened, re-read. The chart kept version-control grep as a live Row 1 option, which is why the correction cost no re-walk here. HOLDS.

5. THE MACHINE ITSELF — verified, because this gate could not be reached without it. The reopen that produced this re-fill exposed a second defect: the re-arm added after the first deadlock handed back join fuel for the state it was activating, so the state re-activated itself on completion. The owner saw it on the board as two sequential states live at once. Fixed, covered by a fifth test whose fixture gives the reopened state an inbound edge — the exact gap that let the first fix ship broken — and promoted (c30f023, 221 passed / 0 failed in trunk).
   Also verified and worth stating: the promotion refused this fix twice, correctly, on a genuine red in trunk. Isolated by running trunk's battery twice (run-d022c8e892a2): 220/220 green with the live session's admission scrubbed, 219/220 with it inherited. The suite runner was verifying against an already-admitted session, so a test asserting that an unadmitted call is refused saw the wrong world. Fixed in the same promotion.

A BLESS IS NOT PROOF: gate_requirements passed, and its register was re-read here for the criteria lineage rather than treated as settled.
payload.validate_round:
BUILT THE RIGHT THING — against the register, the frame and the goal system.

WHAT IS MISSING: nothing this gate must carry. One thing is now KNOWN that was not: X2 cannot search outside a repository, which narrows R7 (outside sources addressed by declared name) and need N1 (read any source the process mandates) if X2 converges. Recorded in the front and in the feasibility check, and handed to M5 as part of the trade rather than resolved here — this gate blesses a front, not a winner.

WHAT IS WRONG: nothing outstanding. The false veto is retracted, and the retraction stands beside the claim in the record.

WHAT IS OUT OF SCOPE: nothing. All ten chart rows sit inside draw_context's boundary. Row 6 option (c), a separate review sub-machine, was pruned precisely BECAUSE it would change the machine's shape, which the excluded list forbids — an excluded item doing real work rather than decorating the record.

AGAINST THE REGISTER: R3 (context in the same call) is satisfied by both survivors — X1 natively, X2 with context alongside --untracked, both probed. R5 and R6 identically. R14's mechanism remains open inside both, exactly as gate_requirements predicted, and goes to M5 as a spike rather than being settled by wording.

ASKS NO CHECK COVERED: none new. C9 exists so measured local failures have a channel into a decision, and this milestone is the test of it — C9 is what re-scored X2 from 2 to 4 once the contradiction turned out to be mine.

AGAINST THE GOAL SYSTEM: G5 held again, and at a cost worth naming. The required rounds produced the correction, and carrying out the correction exposed two engine defects and one false red. That is four separate findings from one gate's review, none of which came from care. G1 (the lane wins on merit) took the hit — this gate cost two reopens of the machine's own code and three promotions. The ruling stands, but the cost is real and is not being written off as free.
payload.redteam_round:
THE OPPOSING CASE, in increasing strictness.

FIRST: the front is now two candidates and X1 leads by twelve weighted points. That is a foregone conclusion wearing a Pareto front, and keeping X2 alive is politeness rather than set-based design. REBUTTED, and with the specific reason the objection is inverted: X2 WINS a criterion outright — installability, 5 against 4 — and there is no weighting of the declared criteria under which it is dominated. A candidate that wins a criterion is on the front by definition, and the totals are recorded precisely so nobody mistakes them for the decision. I also note that eliminating X2 would be convenient for me, since it would restore my original conclusion by a different route, and that is exactly the move the sycophancy guard names.

SECOND, STRICTER: this gate has now been through a probe that overturned it, and the re-fill it ordered surfaced ANOTHER fact nobody knew (X2 cannot search a non-repository source). If two passes and one probe were not enough to establish the basic capabilities of two candidates, what makes the third pass sufficient? Honestly: nothing structural. What I can say is that the remaining claims are now of a different KIND — the load-bearing ones are probed (untracked visibility, ignore-rule reach, output shape, ref search, the PATH absence), and what remains unprobed is scoped and named (the guidance selector, routed to a spike). The first two passes rested on claims that were plausible and untested; this one rests on runs with references. That is not a guarantee, it is a change in the class of risk, and it is the honest claim rather than the comfortable one.

THIRD, STRICTEST: this milestone chose an architecture whose implementation ALREADY EXISTS in trunk. The searcher, the promotion, the reopen — all built before this gate. A candidate evaluation whose winner is already deployed is not an evaluation. This is the same objection gate_requirements answered on the requirements, and it is stronger here, because M4 is where a choice is supposed to be genuinely open. WHAT I CAN SAY AGAINST IT: the choice being blessed here is a FRONT, not a winner, and X2 — the candidate that is NOT built — is on it. If M5 converges on X2, the built searcher goes. That is a real possibility and not a rhetorical one: X2 wins installability, which is the owner's standing bar. WHAT I CANNOT SAY: that the existing implementation exerts no pull. It does, and the only counterweight available is that this front's two survivors differ in a way the code cannot settle, so M5 has to decide something the implementation cannot pre-empt.

CITED RUBRIC: this state's killer — at least two viable candidates survive, or the no-alternatives case is argued — plus the set-based rule that convergence happens at M5 and no winner is picked here. The operative test is whether every elimination rests on a MEASURED property. X3's does (semantic selection has no ground truth here — a property of the situation). X2's did not, which is why it is back.

KILL-CRITERION for PASS: that a candidate on the front is not actually viable — that some capability either survivor needs is missing rather than merely weaker. Looked for it by walking all ten use cases against both. X2's non-repository gap is the closest and it does NOT meet the criterion: R7's obligation is that outside sources are addressed by declared name and read, and reading does not require searching. Named in the front so M5 weighs it rather than discovering it. Not met.
SECOND KILL-CRITERION: that the correction which produced this front is itself unsound — that --untracked has a catch making X2's freshness only nominal. Probed three ways: it finds the unstaged file with line numbers; context works alongside; and it respects ignore rules by default while remaining overridable. Not met.
THIRD, on the other side — what would make another REOPEN right: a further unprobed load-bearing claim in the evidence. I went looking. The remaining unprobed claims are the guidance selector's behaviour (explicitly routed to a spike, not asserted) and the structure metrics (counted from the allocation, not measured against anything). Neither is a claim about the world dressed as an observation, which is the failure mode that reopened this gate twice.

HONEST WEAKNESS: I am the author of everything under review, and this gate has now corrected me twice. The pattern across the iteration is four gates and four defects, all found by required rounds rather than by care. The register's answer — move what can be checked into the mechanical half — is the right one, and it is not available for judgements like 'is this candidate viable'. Reviewer independence remains the missing control and remains unfixable here.
payload.verdict:
PASS.

All five acceptance items hold, and the killer is met by its FIRST branch: two viable candidates survive.
  The front is {X1 fit-per-job, X2 one-searcher}, neither dominating, with the trade stated in one line so M5 inherits a question rather than a preference.
  Every candidate allocates all 36 functions; the two load-bearing interfaces are identical across all three and recorded.
  Nine criteria trace to requirements or named tensions, with the two rewritten or added weights defended rather than listed.
  Every elimination is reasoned, and the one retraction stands beside the claim it replaces.
  Both survivors' feasibility rests on probes; the two unknowns flagged at the last review are settled, one in X2's favour and one against.

NO OVERRIDES.

RECORDED WITH THE PASS:
- This gate reopened once, on its own review, because it had eliminated a candidate on a claim nobody probed. The re-walk restored the candidate AND found a further capability gap in it that two prior passes had missed — evidence that the reopen was substantive rather than procedural.
- Carrying out that reopen exposed a second defect in the machine: the re-arm from the first reopen fix handed back join fuel for the state it was activating, so the state re-activated itself and the walk stopped. The owner saw it on the board before I did. Fixed, five tests, promoted as c30f023 with 221 passed / 0 failed in trunk.
- The promotion refused that fix twice on a genuine red, isolated by running trunk's battery with and without the live session's admission: 220/220 scrubbed against 219/220 inherited. The suite runner was verifying against an admitted session. Fixed in the same promotion.
- The promotion cannot deliver a fix to itself, since it runs trunk's copy of its own code. Named by the owner and logged (note-bbbe848d102d) as work for the next iteration, with the five distinct diagnosis failures from this session as its requirement list.
- X2 cannot search a source that is not a repository. It narrows R7 and need N1 if X2 converges, and M5 must weigh it.

The front is blessed. No winner is picked here. M5 converges.
